tts_summary: This is an earnings-focused note covering two names — Cleveland-Cliffs and Fifth Third Bancorp — with no broad macro or Fed commentary included in this edition. Let's get right into it. Cleveland-Cliffs is the big story here. The steel producer beat third-quarter estimates on both earnings per share and EBITDA — coming in at 28 cents versus the 22-cent consensus, and EBITDA of $612 million versus $592 million expected. Management said average selling prices, volumes, and unit costs were all moving in the right direction simultaneously, which is a clean setup. Fourth-quarter EBITDA guidance of roughly $715 million also clears the Street's $671 million estimate. But the real headline is the 2027 EBITDA outlook — north of $4 billion versus a consensus sitting around $2.5 billion. That is a $1.5 billion-plus gap, and it's not a rounding error. Management credited the trade environment, noting imports remain well below historical levels, lead times are extended, and customers are increasingly valuing reliable domestic supply chains. Several growth initiatives are tracking ahead of expectations. This is a materially bullish print and the 2027 guide could force a significant consensus reset. Watch for analyst upgrades and price target revisions as the Street digests that long-dated number. On the regional bank side, Fifth Third reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.13 versus the $1.08 estimate — a modest beat. The outperformance came from cost discipline, with the efficiency ratio improving 250 basis points on an adjusted basis, and lower provisions at $122 million versus roughly $158 million expected. Revenue was a touch light due to non-interest income coming in slightly below plan. Fourth-quarter guidance was essentially in line — net interest income and expenses a bit better, non-interest income a touch worse. Adam's bottom line on Fifth Third is straightforward: regional banks have had a boring, inline third-quarter season, and this result fits that pattern perfectly. No fireworks, no red flags. Directionally, Cleveland-Cliffs is the actionable name today — the 2027 guide is the kind of number that can re-rate a stock if the market believes it. Fifth Third is a hold-the-line type print with no clear catalyst in either direction.
